basis: NBA players returned an average of 372.5 days after ACL reconstruction (26 players, 84% returned). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average.

NBA players returned an average of 311 days (SD 101) after surgical repair of a complete Achilles rupture (25 players, 1996-2017; 80% returned). Fast end = average minus one SD. A larger study found 72% returned, after 11.2 months on average.
NBA players who had surgery for shoulder instability returned after an average of 19 weeks (50 players). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average.

NBA players missed a median of 17 games (about 5 weeks) after surgery for an isolated meniscus tear (47 players, 2010-2023; 91% returned). That fits a meniscectomy; a meniscus repair can take months, and the report rarely says which, so there's no latest return and it can be season-ending. Fast end = 80% of the median.

NBA players returned an average of 9.8 weeks (69 days) after surgery for a Jones (fifth metatarsal) fracture (10 players). Fast end = 80% of the average. The study gives no spread, so the latest return is a slow recovery of 1.5 times the average (103 days). Applied to foot fractures only.

Pro athletes in the four major US leagues returned an average of 287 days (about 41 weeks) after a traumatic tibial fracture (24 athletes, 2015-2023; the 3 NBA players averaged 315 days). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average. A typical recovery takes most of a season, so there's no latest return and it can be season-ending. Also used for 'lower leg' fractures, which in basketball usually involve the tibia.

NFL players missed an average of 100.5 days (SD 61.7) after a distal fibula fracture (214 fractures, 2000-2014; 90% returned): 124 days with surgery, 75 without, and the injury report rarely says which. Fast end = average minus one SD; latest return = average plus one SD.

NFL players missed an average of 132 days (SD 71) when a fibula fracture came with an ankle dislocation, a medial malleolus fracture or a distal tibia fracture (38 players, 2000-2014; 95% returned). Fast end = average minus one SD; latest return = average plus one SD. Applied to ankle dislocations and fracture-dislocations only.

NBA players returned an average of 44.8 days (16 games) after a hand fracture (173 fractures, 2003-2023: carpal, metacarpal and finger bones). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average and the latest return is a slow recovery of 1.5 times it. Not applied to finger or thumb fractures, which players often play through.

NBA players returned an average of 56.4 days (21 games) after a carpal (wrist bone) fracture, the slowest hand fractures (35 of 173, 2003-2023; 43% had surgery). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average and the latest return is a slow recovery of 1.5 times it.

NBA players returned an average of 2.8 months (about 84 days) after a lumbar discectomy or microdiscectomy (7 players, 6 returned). No spread reported, so the fast end is 80% of the average and the latest return is a slow recovery of 1.5 times it. The report rarely says what kind of back surgery it was; a spinal fusion would take longer.

NFL players returned a median of 11.4 months (interquartile range 9.7-12.6) after a patellar tendon tear (45 players; 58% returned). Fast end = the lower quartile (9.7 months). In the NBA, 3 of 12 players with operative patellar tendon tears never returned, so there's no latest return and it can be season-ending.
